title: Ingenua in Controversias Evangelicorum (Prefatio + Crimina defenses + Part I Protheoria through Coena Domini, Post Lutherum Controv. III-XIII + XV Tolerantia tip, and Hexades Annotationum Prooemium H.I-§.III + Annotatio I §.I-§.IX + J.X + §.XI + §.XII + §.XIII + §.XIV + Decem Theses / Francus + Annotatio II §.I-§.VI + Annotatio III §.I–§.VII (Marburg + Wittenberg + Francofurtanum + Heidelbergense + Sendomiriense + Lipsiacum + Cassellanum) tip)
author: Samuel Strimesius
period: 1708 (Frankfurt an der Oder; Reformed Viadrina faculty)
edition: Ingenua in Controversias Evangelicorum (Francofurti ad Viadrum: Jer. Schrey & J. C. Hartmann, 1708). Google Books 3epYAAAAcAAJ (ONB). Densify: prior tip through Annotatio III §.VI Lipsiacum / Frankfurt Decretum close (§230), plus Annotatio III §.VII Cassellanum molimen (three peculiarities) close before §.VIII (Hexades print pp. 90-91 / PDF ~268-280) (not Annotatio III §.VIII+ fruits; not Prefatio silence reasons; not Hexades theses body; not whole Controversiae; not whole folio).
blurb: Samuel Strimesius — Prefatio through Controversiae Post Lutherum Controv. III-XIII + XV Tolerantia, Hexades Annotationum Prooemium and Annotatio I through Decem Theses / Francus plus Annotatio II §.I-§.VI and Annotatio III §.I–§.VII (through Cassellanum 1661) from Ingenua in Controversias Evangelicorum (Frankfurt an der Oder, 1708). Honest partial; Prefatio silence reasons, Annotatio III §.VIII+ fruits / §.IX+, Hexades theses body, deeper Controversiae / Part II remain.
era_note: Strimesius wrote in the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries as Reformed doctor of theology and primary preacher in the church and university at Frankfurt an der Oder (Viadrina). This is not a patristic work. It is a public-domain Latin Reformed / Frankfurt (Oder) faculty retrieval on the same Fathers-site pipeline. The 1708 Schrey & Hartmann Latin is public domain. Do not treat the site as ante-Nicene only.
first_english_note: No complete public-domain English of this 1708 Latin Ingenua was locked as reading text. Modern AI English was not used. This is a new rendering from locked Latin for Prefatio §I–II, Crimina defenses, Part I Protheoria through Coena Domini and Post Lutherum Controv. III–XIII + XV Tolerantia only.

text_history.method: English follows the locked 1708 Francofurti ad Viadrum Latin of Prefatio §I–II, Crimina defenses through III, Part I Protheoria through Controversiae Obices/Historia/Varii gradus, Formula Discord/Disparitas, Ulterius confirmatur / Classes / Formula protest / triplex differentia, Coena Domini Controversiae Priores through Precariae Hypotheses (Controv. print pp. 34–40), Controversiae Post Lutherum Natae Controv. III–XV tip (providence through De Tolerantia mutua; Controv. print pp. 40–78), Hexades Annotationum Prooemium H.I–§.III (Hexades print pp. 1–4 / PDF ~182–185), and Annotatio I De Augustana Confessione §.I–§.VIII tip (Hexades print pp. 5–24+ / PDF ~186–205+), reconstructed from Google Books PDF page images (ONB copy, id 3epYAAAAcAAJ) with pdftotext as check. No modern English was copied. Sister Halle digitization of Ingenua in Arminianismum (DOI 10.25673/65287) remains Anubis-blocked — skipped; Controversias only. Prefatio silence reasons, Annotatio I §.IX+, Hexades theses body beyond §.VIII, and remainder of Controversiae / folio remain.
